analysis.investment_thesis: Garware Hi-Tech Films is a genuinely improving business — near-zero debt, expanding margins, 40% net profit CAGR over 9 years — but at a trailing earnings yield of ~4.8% (EBIT ₹441 Cr / EV ~₹9,172 Cr), it fails the Magic Formula's minimum 6% threshold. The business is good but the price already reflects that quality, leaving insufficient margin of safety.
key_strengths: Return on Capital ~20% (ROCE 20.6%) — borderline 'good business' by Magic Formula standards, with consistent expansion
Essentially debt-free (D/E 0.01, borrowings ₹18 Cr vs equity ₹2,506 Cr), with ₹110 Cr cash — fortress balance sheet
Operating leverage is real: revenue CAGR 10.5% drove EBIT CAGR 20.7% and net profit CAGR 40% over 9 years
key_risks: Earnings yield ~4.8% (EBIT/EV) is below Magic Formula's 6% floor — you're paying a full price for quality
Operating margin of only 12.75% is thin for specialty films; any raw material (PET/chemicals) cost spike compresses EBIT sharply
Revenue concentration risk — significant US export exposure means USD/INR and US tariff/trade policy are uncontrolled variables
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 21.7x and P/E of 30x price in continued high growth — any deceleration from ₹2,109 Cr revenue base re-rates this stock sharply downward
Other Income of ₹54 Cr (FY25) is ~16% of net profit — inflating reported earnings; stripping this, core earnings yield worsens further
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Garware: EBIT FY25 = ₹441 Cr; Enterprise Value = Market Cap (₹9,267 Cr) + Debt (₹15 Cr) − Cash (₹110 Cr) = ~₹9,172 Cr. Earnings Yield = 4.8% — below the 6% minimum threshold. ROCE of 20.6% barely clears the Magic Formula's 20% "good business" bar. When both metrics need to be high, one failing (cheapness) means this stock doesn't make the cut. On a forward basis (implied FY26 net profit ~₹424 Cr using forward P/E 21.87), EBIT might reach ~₹550 Cr, pushing earnings yield to ~6.0% — barely at threshold, and only if the growth materialises.

The business itself is admirable: debt elimination over a decade (finance costs collapsed from ₹44 Cr to ₹9 Cr), FCF positive 5/5 years (₹276 Cr in FY25), and genuine margin expansion in paint protection and specialty films. But "good business" and "good investment" diverge at the wrong price. At P/B of 3.7x and EV/EBITDA of 21.7x, the market has already priced in the quality. Greenblatt's formula demands we wait for the same quality at a cheaper price — this stock needs to either de-rate to ₹2,800–3,000 (earnings yield ~6.5%+) or grow earnings another 30–40% before the math compels action.
